articles.title: Courtois: "¿Vinicius? Sólo conozco a dos futbolistas que siempre están a su mejor nivel"
articles.standfirst: El portero belga analizó la victoria del Madrid ante el Leipzig en el Bernabéu
articles.summary: El portero belga analizó la victoria del Madrid ante el Leipzig en el Bernabéu
articles.body: Thibaut Courtois atendió a los medios de comunicación en la zona mixta del Santiago Bernabéu tras la victoria del Madrid (4-1) frente al RB Leipzig en la fase de liga de la Champions League. El guardameta belga, uno de los mejores del partido, analizó el estado de forma del equipo de cara al inminente Clásico liguero, defendió el rendimiento de su compañero Vinicius frente a las críticas y prefirió mantener un voto de confianza hacia la honestidad del colectivo arbitral y la herramienta del VAR. Victoria antes del Clásico: "Al final yo creo que hemos jugado buenos partidos, buenas victorias, una buena remontada en Roma y al final estamos con confianza para lo que viene y sabemos que va a ser un partido duro, pero si queremos recortar puntos en la Liga habrá que ir a ganar el partido". ¿Es favorito el Barça?: "Al final nunca se sabe hasta que juegas el partido ahí, yo creo que estamos bien, estamos con confianza y al final en la Liga han estado muy bien, pero yo confío en nuestro equipo que podamos ir a ganar. Es verdad que es en su casa, es un partido diferente cuando vas de visitante, pero yo confío en nuestro equipo y para mí los Clásicos, aunque a veces llega un equipo mejor que otro, para mí siempre son 50-50". Vinicius: "No, yo creo que está en busca de su mejor versión y estoy seguro que llegará con el apoyo del equipo, de la afición y creo que ha hecho un partido bueno, le he visto con acciones, con peligro y al final no siempre te salen las cosas. Un jugador que está cada temporada a su mejor nivel, ahora que yo solo conozco a dos, que son Cristiano y Messi, que los he visto casi cada año en su mejor nivel y aún así se les han criticado en varios momentos a dos de los más grandes de la historia. Al final es fútbol, yo creo que Vinicius es alguien que lleva nueve años jugando casi todo y por eso nosotros tenemos que ayudarle a buscar esa mejor versión, pero él es el primer entrenador que está contento, feliz y buscando su mejor versión. Dificultades fuera de casa: "En casa y fuera siempre son partidos diferentes y nos ha costado más hacer los partidos fuera, como en España, Roma, Elche y luego las dos derrotas de Betis, yo creo que a Betis merecimos más, ahí perdimos pero hicimos un buen partido. Es verdad que fuera de casa hay que mejorar, pero aún así creo que nos estamos haciendo bien ahora en la vuelta después del parón y estaremos con ganas del domingo y con lo que viene, porque ahora hay cuatro partidos fuera de casa y si no queremos desengancharnos de la liga, pues son tres partidos". ¿Tenéis miedo del arbitraje este fin semana?: "No, porque al final yo confío en los árbitros, confío que ellos van con la conciencia de hacer lo que ellos pueden hacer y que al final son humanos, pueden hacer errores, pero bueno, esperamos que no siempre son errores para un lado y no para otro. Y que cuando entre el VAR sean por cosas por las que de verdad vino el VAR. Desde 2018 que se introdujo era para cosas muy claras y yo siento que en la Liga entran demasiado. Y cosas que cuentan a principio de temporada, que nos comemos una hora de charla de los árbitros para que luego a la semana se estén equivocando y haciendo cosas al revés, pero yo como humano y como persona optimista, yo quiero creer que siempre van honestos al campo y como te digo, puedes equivocarte y por eso está el VAR, pero ya está".

articles.title: Saka injury 'does not look good' - how will Arsenal cope?
articles.summary: Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the Champions League draw with Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".
articles.body:
Mikel Arteta says the quadriceps injury Arsenal's Bukayo Saka picked up in the 2-2 Champions League draw against Bayern Munich "does not look good at all".

The 25-year-old winger went down in the 10th minute at Allianz Arena - attempting to play a pass with nobody around him - and had to be replaced by Eberechi Eze, who went on to score the opening goal.

"They are a bit concerned. A player who has to come off with a really sharp pain is never good news but we have to wait and see," Arteta told TNT Sports.

Saka has had fitness issues in recent months and his game time was managed at the end of last season, as well as with England at the World Cup, because of an Achilles injury he picked up in March.

He missed the March international break and seven games for the Gunners, but returned to help them lift the Premier League title for the first time in 22 years.

Saka started the Champions League final defeat by Paris St-Germain but was substituted after 54 minutes, and only started three of England's eight games at the World Cup - scoring a hat-trick in the 6-4 third-place win over France.

The forward also had surgery on a hamstring injury he picked up in December 2024, which kept him out for 101 days in the 2024-25 season.

He made 49 appearances as Arsenal won the title last term, despite a stop-start season - as well as the Achilles issue, he pulled out of the warm-up against Leeds with a hip injury in January and a hamstring problem kept him out for about four weeks.

But he remains vital to the Gunners, whose win percentage is notably more impressive with him in the team.

Despite the loss of Saka early on in the game, Arsenal still produced a good performance and could have won the match late on after Declan Rice's late equaliser.

"The only negative is seeing one of their star players, Saka, having to pull up with an injury early in the first half," said Champions League Match of the Day pundit Nedum Onuoha.

"He was lying on the floor with his hand up and he knew he was in a bit of trouble, so now the concern will be how long he is out for.

"It's not necessarily something that means the team will struggle heavily, but there is a reason why he is regarded as one of the best players in this Arsenal team and is seen as being important for them."

After Saka's withdrawal Noni Madueke, who had started on the left wing, switched to the right and looked bright, while Eze scored the opening goal from the left after coming off the bench.

"This is one of the reasons their squad has been built the way it has been and I think Madueke and Eze did well on the wings today after Saka came off," added Onuoha.

"In terms of options, at this moment in time for Arsenal, it is not going to be an issue - they will miss the star power that he has, they still have plenty of other wide players who can step up and do the job while they wait for him to come back."

Arsenal's style of play has been criticised this season but, even before Saka's withdrawal, the Gunners played on the front foot and enjoyed more possession than their German opponents.

Losing Saka, who has scored four goals in 11 appearances in all competitions, will be tough to deal with.

But the Gunners have invested heavily in their squad over the past two summer transfer windows and have options.

Madueke can play on both wings, while summer signing Christos Tzolis - although currently out with a hamstring injury - has started the season well.

The Gunners also have 16-year-old Max Dowman as an attacking option, and the youngster has already shown that he can have an impact for the senior side after scoring in the Premier League last season.

Arteta, who was asked what the rest of the forward line will need to do in Saka's absence, said he was pleased with what he saw against Bayern.

"I think Ebs [Eze] had a great game. Not only the ball, but the actions. His overall performance, I think his commitment without the ball as well," he said.

"And when the other ones come in, I think they really contributed to this. First of all, the energy.

"And then to bring different tools that the team needed in that moment to get something out of the game. So, very pleased again."
authors: Alex Howell - Arsenal reporter in Munich

articles.title: How USC would have fared retroactively with a 24-team playoff
articles.summary: A 24-team playoff is reportedly coming to college football as soon as next season. Had it been introduced in 2014, which years would USC have made it?
articles.body:
Last week, it was revealed that a 24-team playoff is all but certainly coming to college football. Despite the proposal being extremely unpopular , the new system is reportedly set to take effect as soon as next year.

So how would this affect USC? Let's take a look back at the 12-year history of the College Football Playoff and see which years the Trojans would have made the field:

USC would have been the final team to make the playoff, squeaking in as the No. 24 seed. The Trojans would have visited No. 9 seed Ole Miss in a first round matchup.

Coming in at No. 25 in the final College Football Playoff rankings, USC would have been the first team out of the field.

USC would have been the No. 9 seed, just missing out on a first round bye. The Trojans would have hosted No. 24 seed Temple in a first round game at the Coliseum.

This time, USC would have gotten a bye, earning the No. 8 seed. The Trojans would have hosted a second round game against the winner of the first round matchup between No. 9 seed Penn State and No. 24 seed NC State.

After a horrific 5-7 season, USC would not have even come close to making the playoff.

The Trojans would have been the No. 22 seed and visited No. 11 seed Utah in a first round game. It would have been a rematch of a September meeting between the two teams at the Coliseum, which USC won 30-23.

The No. 17 seed Trojans would have visited No. 16 seed BYU in a first round game.

This was the worst USC football team of the modern era, with the Trojans finishing 4-8. They could have expanded the playoff to 48 and this team still would not have been worthy of a spot.

USC would have made it back to the playoff in 2022 as the No. 10 seed. The Trojans would have welcomed No. 23 seed NC State to the Coliseum for a first round matchup.

After starting the year 6-0, USC went 1-5 in its final six regular season games, leading to the Trojans missing the playoff.

A 6-6 regular season would have seen the Trojans not even sniff the bracket for the third time in four years.

USC would have returned to the playoff for the first time in three years as the No. 16 seed. The Trojans would have hosted No. 17 seed Arizona in a first round game at the Coliseum.

In 12 years, USC would have made the 24-team playoff seven times. The Trojans would have been a top eight seed once, between No. 9 and No. 16 three times, and been one of the final eight teams in three times.

articles.title: 📋 Palmeiras line-up confirmed to face Fluminense
articles.summary: The time has come!Palmeiras and Fluminense face off on Wednesday night (21) in the second leg of their Copa Libertadores semifinal.Kickoff is coming up at 9:...
articles.body:
Palmeiras and Fluminense face off on Wednesday night (21) in the second leg of their Copa Libertadores semifinal.

Kickoff is coming up at 9:30 p.m. (Brasília time) at Nubank.

The other finalist will be decided on Thursday (22), when Flamengo face Estudiantes after a 0–0 draw in the first leg.

Uruguayan referee Esteban Ostojich will officiate.

TV Globo, ge tv and Paramount+ will broadcast the match.

After winning 2–1 at the Maracanã, Verdão only need a draw in front of their home fans.

They are aiming to reach their eighth Libertadores final and chase a fourth title.

Tricolor need to win by two goals to advance in regulation time.

A one-goal win would send the tie to a penalty shootout.

They are seeking their third Libertadores final and a second title.

Abel Ferreira has Giay and Gustavo Gómez available again after they served suspensions in the Brasileirão.

Marlon Freitas and Arias, who were rested for part of the match against Athletico, also return to the starting lineup.

One reason for optimism is their good form since the last international break.

They have picked up four wins while playing good football.

Marcão welcomes back the players who were rested for part of the match against Santos.

Renê is expected to reclaim his starting spot at left-back.

There is a question mark in attack over whether Canobbio or Serna will start.

The big mystery surrounding Martinelli's involvement, however, has been resolved.

The No. 8—who sprained his knee in the first leg—has been named in the squad, but is not guaranteed a place in the starting XI.

After a good run, Flu now need to turn things around following three straight defeats.

articles.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany delivers health update after Arsenal clash
articles.summary: The FC Bayern bossman battled illness heading into the big Champions League showdown this week.
articles.body:
Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany was waylaid this week by a viral infection with symptoms bothersome enough that it even affected his ability to move around on the sidelines in last weekend's match against RB Leipzig.

The Bavarians romped all over the Red Bull club, 6-1, but Kompany cut a subdued figure as he dealt with the effects of whatever virus he had contracted, which aggravated an old hip injury. It was bad enough that there were reports surfacing about Bayern's contingency plans—with assistant Aaron Danks taking charge as sideline gesticulator-in-chief should Kompany be a no-go for this week's hotly anticipated Champions League clash against Premier League champion Arsenal.

Thankfully, Kompany recovered in time to prowl the sidelines himself on Wednesday, and was even able to jump up and gesture at the officials following a questionable call or two. The contest, a high-quality affair with scintillating moments of brilliance from both sides, ended in a 2-2 draw .

"I'm doing better," Kompany shared at his post-match press conference (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ). "It's a normal human thing. As a coach, you want to do everything by yourself. I didn't listen to my body, and at some point my body told me: 'Stop now, man!' …that was it.

"Now I'm feeling better, otherwise I wouldn't be here."

PSA aside: it is respiratory virus season after all, and all sorts of nasties are floating around. It's not too late to go get your flu and other shots—for yourself and the community!
